findings.title: Harmonized vote shares use total_votes (about valid votes) as denominator; codebook and unharm file use number_voters
findings.description: The codebook (federal section and 'Denominators and result versions' table) and data_pipeline.md state that federal municipality shares are proportions of number_voters, and that share*number_voters gives party counts. This is true for federal_muni_unharm (and the raw-derived data), but in harm_21 and harm_25 the shares are recomputed as party/total_votes (script 02_federal_muni_harm_21.R line 847, 03_federal_muni_harm_25.R line 539), and total_votes is approximately valid_votes. A user who follows the codebook on harm files gets party counts overstated by 0.5-1.7% nationally (CSU up to 0.85%, CDU up to 1.67%), and unharm vs harm shares for the same municipality differ systematically (about 1% in 2021, 0.6% in 2025, up to 1.7% in 2005). Party shares in harm sum to exactly 1 while unharm shares sum to valid_votes/number_voters (about 0.9-0.99).
findings.evidence: Kiel 01001000 2021: raw cdu=7152 votes; unharm cdu=0.139475 (x number_voters 51278 = 7152); harm_21 cdu=0.1407375 (x valid 50818 = 7152; x number_voters = 7217). National 2021 CDU: unharm sum(cdu*number_voters)=8,775,478 (official 8,775,471); harm_21 sum(cdu*number_voters)=8,858,871 (+0.95%) but sum(cdu*total_votes)=8,775,478. Overstatement of sum(share*number_voters) vs unharm by year (CDU %): 1990 1.25, 1994 1.47, 1998 1.39, 2002 1.33, 2005 1.67, 2009 1.54, 2013 1.43, 2017 1.05, 2021 -0.95 (sign change because 2021/2025 use different residual), 2025 0.61. Median party-share sum: unharm 0.897 (2021) vs harm 0.909 / 1.0 over all party columns.
findings.suggested_fix: Either document explicitly that unharm shares are of number_voters while harm shares are of valid votes (total_votes), or recompute harm shares with number_voters so the three files share one convention; update codebook table row 'Federal county and municipality share files'.
findings.already_known: no (codebook asserts number_voters for all municipality files)

verification.notes: Re-ran. Kiel 01001000 2021: unharm cdu*number_voters = valid-vote-equivalent matches; harm_21 total_votes==valid_votes==50818 and cdu share is of total_votes. National CDU sum(share*number_voters): 2005 unharm 13,136,749 vs harm 13,356,668 (+1.67%); 2017 12,447,668 vs 12,578,833 (+1.05%); 2021 8,775,478 vs 8,858,871 (+0.95%, positive, not a sign change); 2025 harm_25 11,196,405 vs 11,264,221 (+0.61%). Using total_votes recovers the unharm figure exactly. Codebook (Denominators table and Federal section) states number_voters for all federal municipality files and says shares need not sum to 1, which is false for harm. Real documentation contradiction, but the effect is a ~1% scaling and a denominator convention, so medium rather than high.

findings.title: State-level mail-in (Briefwahl) rows are dropped for East German states in 1994, 1998, 2002: 167k-228k votes lost, turnout understated by up to 8pp
findings.description: In federal_muni_raw a single state-level mail-in row (ags xx000999) holds all postal votes for several states. These rows are not allocated and are absent from unharm and harm files. National valid votes are 0.35-0.48% below official in 1994/1998/2002, but the loss is concentrated in Brandenburg, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Sachsen-Anhalt, Thueringen (1.2-8.3% of state votes) and Rheinland-Pfalz/Schleswig-Holstein partly. State aggregates built from unharm/harm are therefore wrong and municipal turnout in these states and years is too low by several points (municipal values are consistent among themselves only if mail-in is ignored).
findings.evidence: National valid votes raw (=official) vs unharm: 1994 47,105,174 vs 46,876,817 (-228,357); 1998 49,308,512 vs 49,101,310 (-207,202); 2002 47,996,480 vs 47,829,890 (-166,590); other years diff <=314. State pct valid lost: 1994 BB 5.85, MV 6.88, ST 1.24(+ others), SN 2.42; 1998 BB 8.33 (row 12000999, 128,486 valid votes), MV 7.17, ST etc; 2002 BB 3.32, ST 3.67, TH 2.12, SN 0.94, BW 0.12. Brandenburg 1998 turnout from unharm sum(number_voters)/sum(eligible_voters_orig)=71.7%, from raw 1,587,152/2,032,303=78.1%. Brandenburg 1994: 67.3% vs 71.5%. harm_21 valid_votes totals equal the (reduced) unharm totals, so the loss propagates.
findings.suggested_fix: Allocate the state-level mail-in rows (county key 12000, 13000, 15000, etc.) to municipalities within the state, or at minimum document that these votes are absent and add the unallocated totals as a separate file or flag. The harm scripts' reconciliation only compares harm to unharm, so it does not detect this.

verification.notes: Re-ran. Raw vs unharm valid votes: 1994 47,105,174 vs 46,876,817; 1998 49,308,512 vs 49,101,310; 2002 47,996,480 vs 47,829,890; 2021 differs by 16. Loss by state: 1994 BB 5.85%, MV 6.88%, SN 2.42%, ST 1.24%; 1998 BB 8.33%, MV 7.17%; 2002 BB 3.32%, ST 3.67%, TH 2.12%, SN 0.94%, BW 0.12%. Raw 12000999 (1998) has 128,486 valid votes; unharm has zero rows ending 999 in 1998. BB 1998 turnout: unharm 71.7% vs raw 78.1%. Rows ending 999 (county-level mail-in aggregates) are flagged flag_briefwahl_agg in raw and codebook, and harmonization_audit_2026-09-16.md lists six county postal totals (12999,13999,14999,15999 in 1994; 12999,13999 in 1998) as excluded, so the exclusion is partly documented. The audit says they 'remain in the unharmonized file', but they are absent from federal_muni_unharm. Impact on state aggregates and turnout is undocumented. Also includes 2002 county 999 rows (e.g. 12065999) beyond the six. Note the finding's wording 'state-level row' is loose: they are county-level aggregates.

findings.title: eligible_voters is inflated by added mail-in voters, and turnout is not number_voters/eligible_voters as documented
findings.description: eligible_voters (post-allocation) equals eligible_voters_orig plus allocated mail-in voters, i.e. mail-in voters are added to the electorate as well as to number_voters. National sums exceed the official electorate in every year (1980 by 11.5%, 1983 0.6%, 2021 2.3%, 2025 2.1%). The turnout column is number_voters/eligible_voters_orig (this matches official national turnout), not number_voters/eligible_voters as the codebook line for turnout states; row-level number_voters/eligible_voters differs from turnout in about 50% of rows (99% in 1980). Users computing turnout or population-weighted electorate size from eligible_voters get wrong values (e.g. 1980 aggregate 79.4% vs official 88.6%).
findings.evidence: Sum eligible_voters vs eligible_voters_orig (=official): 1980 48,223,683 vs 43,231,741; 1990 60,850,387 vs 60,436,560; 2021 62,573,263 vs 61,181,072; 2025 61,782,923 vs 60,510,631. Flensburg 01001000 1980: eligible_orig 67,610, eligible_voters 74,957 (+7,347 = same increment as number_voters 51,102 -> 58,449), turnout 0.8645 = 58,449/67,610 but 58,449/74,957 = 0.78. Juist 03452013 1980: eligible 1,242 -> 1,751 (+41%). Codebook line 55 turnout = number_voters/eligible_voters; data_pipeline.md says eligible_voters_orig. The aggregate eligible_voters ratio >1.05 of orig in 6,796 of 8,493 municipalities in 1980.
findings.suggested_fix: Document that eligible_voters includes allocated mail-in voters and should not be used as the electorate size (use eligible_voters_orig), and correct the codebook turnout definition for federal municipality files; preferably do not add mail-in voters to eligible_voters.
findings.already_known: partially (data_pipeline.md states turnout uses eligible_voters_orig; codebook contradicts and says nothing about the inflation)

verification.notes: Re-ran. Sum eligible_voters vs eligible_voters_orig: 1980 48,223,683 vs 43,231,741; 1990 60,850,387 vs 60,436,560; 2021 62,573,263 vs 61,181,072; 2025 61,782,923 vs 60,510,631. Flensburg 01001000 1980: eligible 74,957 vs orig 67,610, number_voters 58,449, turnout 0.865 = 58,449/67,610. In 2021 only 53% of rows have turnout == number_voters/eligible_voters. Codebook turnout row says number_voters/eligible_voters; data_pipeline.md uses eligible_voters_orig; the codebook mail-in block does document eligible_voters_orig. Documentation gap and misleading column, not a computational error in turnout.

findings.title: 2021 and 2025 have zero-vote rows and municipalities whose votes are reported under another municipality; unbalanced panel and implausible jumps
findings.description: In 2021 (179 rows) and 2025 (47 rows) small municipalities appear with eligible_voters=0, number_voters=0, valid_votes=0, NaN party shares and NA turnout/cdu_csu/far_right (the codebook says NA means no recorded result, but here the vote counts are 0). In addition 144 municipalities present in 2017 have no 2021 row at all (BW, RP 97, MV 9, TH 23, SH 15), so harm_21 has 10,641 municipalities in 2021 vs about 10,787 in other years. Their votes sit in other municipalities with shared polling districts, producing implausible jumps (and shares not attributable to the municipality) with no flag. Votes remain conserved nationally.
findings.evidence: 2021 zero-eligible rows 179, 2025 47 (e.g. 01051008 Bergewöhrden, 01051038 Groven, 01053001 Albsfelde, all valid_votes=0). Missing 2021 rows: 144 ags with 14,625 valid votes in 2017. findings.title: Mail-in over-allocation yields number_voters far above eligible voters in some municipalities; turnout fallback inconsistent with number_voters
findings.description: The proportional mail-in allocation can assign more voters than the municipality has electorate (92 unharm rows with number_voters/eligible_voters_orig>1, 30 of them >1.1, max 3.30). For these rows turnout is overwritten with number_voters_orig/eligible_voters_orig, while vote shares and number_voters still contain the over-allocated values; 119 rows have turnout exactly 1 (capped). Only the generic flag_naive_turnout_above_1 documents it.
findings.evidence: Dobitschen 16077003 2025: eligible_orig 366, number_voters 1,207 (ratio 3.30), turnout reported 0.702; 15089010 2009: eligible_orig 687, number_voters 1,598 (2.33); Kruft 07137057 2025: 2,801 voters vs 2,667 eligible. 63 unharm rows with number_voters > eligible_voters (harm: 13). Rows with turnout==1: 119.
findings.suggested_fix: Document that municipality-level counts in these rows are allocation artifacts; consider capping the allocation or flagging rows where allocated voters exceed the electorate.

verification.notes: Re-ran. 92 unharm rows with number_voters/eligible_voters_orig>1, 30 >1.1, max 3.30. Dobitschen 16077003 2025: eligible_orig 366, number_voters 1,207 (number_voters_orig 257), turnout 0.702. turnout==1 in 119 rows; number_voters>eligible_voters in 63 unharm rows and 13 harm_21 rows. Codebook already mentions allocation artefacts for turnout >1 and flag_naive_turnout_above_1 exists; affects ~0.06% of rows, so low severity.

findings.title: 1957, 1961, 1965 county totals omit postal (Briefwahl) votes; turnout understated by 4-5 pp
findings.description: Postal voting was introduced in 1957. The county raw files for 1957, 1961 and 1965 appear to contain only polling-station votes, so national voters, valid votes and party counts are short by 5-7%, and turnout is far below the published value. From 1969 on, totals match official figures. docs/data_pipeline.md says county data already includes absentee votes, which does not hold for these three years. No codebook caveat exists. Users computing turnout or party vote counts for 1957-1965 get wrong levels.
findings.evidence: 1957: number_voters sum 29,535,800 vs official 31,072,894 (-4.95%); turnout 83.4% vs official 87.8%; CDU count 11,130,349 vs official 11,875,339 (-6.3%); SPD 9,178,234 vs 9,495,571. 1965: number_voters 30,972,272 vs official 33,416,207 (-7.3%); turnout 80.4% vs 86.8%; SPD 12,036,396 vs 12,813,186 (-6.1%); CDU 11,337,007 vs 12,387,562. 1961: turnout 82.7% (same pattern; published about 87.7%, not externally fetched). 1953 (86.0%) and 1969 (86.7%) match.
findings.reproduce: Rscript scratchpad/audit/federal-cty-wkr/c6.R and c8.R (sum(spd*number_voters) by year vs wikipedia Bundestagswahl_1957 / _1965)
findings.suggested_fix: Document the gap in the codebook and fix the data_pipeline.md claim, or add the unallocated postal votes as an explicit row/flag, or set a flag for 1957-1965.

verification.notes: Re-ran with own code on federal_cty_unharm. Sums match the finding: number_voters 1957 29,535,800, 1961 30,958,020, 1965 30,972,272; turnout from eligible/voters 83.4%, 82.7%, 80.4%. Eligible_voters sums equal the official electorate (e.g. 1957 35,400,923), so voters are what is short. 1953 (86.0%) and 1969 (86.7%) are consistent with official values. Official turnout is about 87.8% / 87.7% / 86.8%. This was checked from memory and the finding's figures, not fetched. No mention of 1957-65 or postal votes in the codebook or data_pipeline. data_pipeline.md line 267 says county data already includes absentee votes. federal_cty_harm starts in 1990, so it is unaffected. Postal voting as the cause is plausible but not proven here.

findings.title: Municipality file under-counts East German voters in 2002 (and 1994/1998 Briefwahl) relative to county file
findings.description: Aggregating federal_muni_unharm to 5-digit county reproduces county totals within 0.1% in most years, but 2002 East German counties are short by up to 10.8% of voters, and the national sum is 0.35% below the official total (the county file matches official). In 1994 and 1998 the municipality file has no equivalent of the four '999' Briefwahl aggregate rows (about 230k and 209k voters). Users who build county panels from the municipality file get downward-biased turnout and vote counts in East German counties.
findings.suggested_fix: Allocate the unassigned East German Briefwahl votes in the municipality pipeline for 2002 (and 1994/1998) or document the gap; check the 1980 Osterholz/Verden-type county code mismatch (03254/03255).

verification.notes: Aggregating federal_muni_unharm to 5-digit county vs the county file: 2002 muni 48,415,152 vs 48,582,761 (-0.35%). 52 counties differ by more than 1%, all in states 08, 12, 14, 15, 16. Worst: 16074 -10.8%, 15266 -10.5%, 16065 -7.0%, 12062 -6.8%. 1994 and 1998 national muni sums are 47,508,371 and 49,737,935. The county file's 999 aggregate rows (80,461 / 68,244 / 62,249 / 18,767 voters in 1994; 129,734 / 78,848 in 1998) have no muni counterpart. The codebook documents these as flag_briefwahl_agg on the county file only. The 1980 deviation affects 2 counties, not an extra finding. Severity is medium: the deficit is at most 0.35% nationally, but up to 10.8% in individual East German counties.

findings.title: Allocated eligible_voters column is inflated far above official electorate; pooled turnout from columns is wrong
findings.description: The sum of eligible_voters over municipalities exceeds the official electorate (which eligible_voters_orig and the county file reproduce exactly) in every year, by 0.6% to 11.5%. Dividing number_voters by eligible_voters gives pooled turnout several points too low (1980: 79.4% vs official 88.6%). The county-level maximum is 48% (07235 Trier-Saarburg 2021: 166,226 vs 112,182). The separate turnout column looks plausible (mean 0.895 in 1980), so the inconsistency is between eligible_voters and turnout. The mail-in allocation appears to add eligible electors to municipalities with shared Briefwahl districts without scaling.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not scale allocated electors above the original total, or document that eligible_voters after allocation is not an electorate count and tell users to use eligible_voters_orig for turnout.
findings.already_known: no (codebook describes the _orig columns but not the inflation)

verification.notes: Muni eligible_voters summed over counties vs county/official: 1980 +11.5%, 1983 +0.6%, 1990 +0.7%, 2005 +1.5%, 2013 +1.4%, 2017 +1.8%, 2021 +2.3%, 2025 +2.1%. eligible_voters_orig equals the county total exactly in every year. County extremes in 2021: 07235 has 166,226 vs 112,182 (+48%), 07143 +46.8%, 07331 +42.7%. Pooled number_voters/eligible_voters in 1980 is 0.794, while the turnout column averages 0.895. The codebook describes the _orig columns but does not warn that allocated eligible_voters is inflated. Severity is medium: typical years are under 2.5% and the turnout column is fine, but 1980 and some counties are badly off.

findings.title: Harmonized county file drops 1994 and 1998 East German Briefwahl votes; turnout biased down
findings.description: The 999 Briefwahl aggregate rows (12999, 13999, 14999, 15999 in 1994; 12999, 13999 in 1998) are flagged in federal_cty_unharm but have no counterpart in federal_cty_harm. Harmonized national totals are 0.4-0.5% below official, and turnout in Brandenburg, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Sachsen, Sachsen-Anhalt in those years is understated.
findings.evidence: harm vs unharm number_voters: 1994 47,508,279 vs 47,737,999 (-0.48%); 1998 49,738,504 vs 49,947,087 (-0.42%); valid_votes -0.48% and -0.42%. Rows lost: 1994 4 rows with 80,461/68,244/62,249/18,767 voters; 1998 2 rows with 129,734/78,848. Harm file national turnout 1994 78.6% vs official 79.0%. Other years match to 1e-8.
findings.suggested_fix: Allocate these votes to counties in the affected states or add a note in the codebook that harmonized totals exclude them.
findings.already_known: partly (codebook describes the flag on unharm only)

verification.notes: federal_cty_harm vs federal_cty_unharm number_voters: 1994 47,508,279 vs 47,737,999 (-0.48%); 1998 49,738,504 vs 49,947,087 (-0.42%). All other years match to 1e-8. The 999 rows (flag_briefwahl_agg = 1) exist only in unharm. The codebook notes the flag for the unharm file only.

findings.title: elected_party filled on both erststimme and zweitstimme rows, contradicting codebook
findings.description: Codebook says elected_party is populated on erststimme rows only. It is populated on all 4186 rows and is identical across the two ballot rows, so filtering by stimme is required to count mandates correctly. The values themselves match official Direktmandat counts.

findings.suggested_fix: Fix the codebook text or set elected_party to NA on zweitstimme rows.

verification.notes: table(!is.na(elected_party), stimme) gives 2093 non-NA on erststimme and 2093 on zweitstimme. The codebook says it is populated on erststimme rows only. I did not re-check the Direktmandat counts.

findings.title: Implausible eligible_voters / population ratios in some East German county-years
findings.description: Population (and area) covariates appear mismatched with eligible voters in a few county-years; eligible voters cannot be 95-99% of residents.
findings.suggested_fix: Recheck the population crosswalk for Leipzig-Land (14729), Dessau-Rosslau (15001), Wittenberg (15091) and Sachsen-Anhalt/Thuringia counties.

verification.notes: eligible_voters/population ratio: 29 rows above 0.88, 5 above 0.95. Top rows: 14729 1998 0.989 (pop 235,087 vs eligible 232,518); 15001 2005 0.976; 15001 2002 0.976; 15091 2005 0.952; 14729 1994 0.951. Ratios return to about 0.82-0.86 in other years for the same counties, so the population value is implausible in those years. The cause (crosswalk or interpolation) was not diagnosed.

findings.title: 2025 population and area are copies of 2021
findings.description: population and area for election_year 2025 are identical to 2021 values, but the column appears to be year-specific.

findings.title: flag_unsuccessful_naive_merge is only populated for 2021 and 2025 and is always 0
findings.description: The flag has 3200 NA and 800 zeros (only 2021/2025), so it carries no information and its meaning is unclear.

The codebook defines it only as a fallback-match marker and does not mention that it is NA before 2021. It carries no information as shipped.

findings.title: Inconsistent column names for the same party and identifiers across county and Wahlkreis files
findings.description: Same entities carry different column names, which breaks cross-file code and mixes shares of different denominators.
findings.evidence: cty: x50plus, di_b, pd_h, die_basis, team_todenhoefer, freie_waehler, unabhaengige, buendnis_c; wkr: 50plus, dib, pdh, diebasis, team_todenhofer, freie_wahler, unabhangige, bundnis_c. findings.title: Berlin 2021 and 2023 `gruene` includes Die Grauen; 2023 ranks Gruene ahead of SPD
findings.description: Statewide Gruene share in Berlin is overstated by exactly the Die Grauen vote share, which suggests the party was merged into the gruene column. In 2023 the official result has SPD ahead of Gruene by 53 votes, but GERDA shows Gruene ahead by about 0.4pp.

BE 2023: GERDA 18.82% vs official 18.39% (278,964), diff 0.43pp = DieGrauen 0.43%; SPD 18.39% (279,017). A separate `graue` column holds 0.49% / 0.41%, so the merge is not the Graue column. findings.title: Brandenburg 1999 misses 22% of the electorate and 27% of valid votes; municipal rows corrupt
findings.description: The BB 1999 Landtag election in state_unharm (and thus all three harm versions) sums to far less than the official result. About 51 municipalities are absent and many present rows hold wrong (Amt-level or misallocated) counts. The row carries no source-unreliable flag and is not in source_limitations.csv or the final README.
findings.evidence: Statewide totals unharm vs bundeslaendeR/official: eligible 1,604,122 vs 2,056,834 (-22.0%); voters 813,981 vs 1,116,874 (-27.1%); valid 804,330 vs 1,102,360 (-27.0%). Same totals in ltw_wkr_unharm (wkr zweitstimme, 44 WK): 2,056,834 / 1,116,874 / 1,102,360, so the wkr file is correct. Municipality count: 1,124 in unharm; harm_25 has 362 AGS vs 413 in other BB years (-12%). Jumps within AGS: Letschin 12064274 eligible 4,269 (1994) -> 157 (1999) -> 4,158 (2004); Milmersdorf 12073396 1,603 -> 69 -> 1,487; Schoenwalde-Glien 12063273 4,216 -> 350 -> 6,570; Luebbenau 12066196 17,380 -> 1,487 -> 15,470. 22 AGS in harm_25 BB 1999 have eligible ratio >3x or <1/3 vs adjacent election. Also 12069020 (1999) number_voters 4,529 < valid_votes 5,388 in harm_25 (and 12071294, 840 vs 902). Internal docs/state_pipeline_audit.md says BB 1999 is 27.1% short ('not fixable without re-digitising') but README/codebook/source_limitations.csv do not mention it; TODO.md and issue #7 cover only 1990/1994.
findings.already_known: Partially: docs/state_pipeline_audit.md (internal, 27.1% short, OCR). Not in README, codebook, source_limitations.csv, or GitHub #7 text.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-digitise BB 1999 from the ltw_wkr or official Amt/Gemeinde tables, or at minimum add BB 1999 to source_limitations.csv with flag_source_unreliable=1 and a README entry.

verification.already_known: Partly: internal docs/state_pipeline_audit.md says BB 1999 is 27.1% short from OCR and not fixable without re-digitising. Not in README or source_limitations.
verification.notes: Re-ran. unharm BB 1999: 1124 rows, eligible 1,604,122, voters 813,981, valid 804,330. ltw_wkr_unharm (44 WK, zweitstimme) gives 2,056,834 / 1,116,874 / 1,102,360. bundeslaendeR valid_votes is 1,102,360, so unharm is -27.04% on valid and -22.0% on eligible. harm_25 has only 362 AGS for BB 1999. Magnitudes are exact.

findings.evidence: Against bundeslaendeR (>=1.5% and column exists elsewhere): Rep BY 1990 4.85% (and rep column empty for BY, see SH-05), Rep NI 1994 3.74%, BIW HB 2015 3.23% and 2019 2.44% (biw populated only for 2011 3.69%), DVU HB 1999 3.03%, 2003 2.28%, 2007 2.73%, PRO/Schill HB 2003 4.4%, Piraten HB 2011 1.90%, 2015 1.52%, SH 2009 1.80%, DiePartei HB 2015 1.87%, 2019 1.66%, Tierschutzpartei SL 2022 2.30%, ST 2011 1.58%, FW SL 2022 1.69%, WASG NW 2005 2.21%, NPD HB 2011 1.56%, NPD SH 2005 1.93%. `other` for HB 2003 = 9.05%, HB 2015 = 8.00%, HB 2019 = 7.59%. verification.notes: Spot-checked: HB 2003 DVU is 2.28% official but the dvu column is 0 and other is 9.05%; HB 2015 and 2019 BIW are 3.23% and 2.44% with biw 0 and other 8.00% and 7.59%; SL 2022 Tierschutz is 2.30% with tierschutz 0 and other 8.77%. findings.title: SH 2008/2013 (and likely 1994-2003) party shares for kreisangehoerige municipalities are Kreistag results, not Gemeinderat results
findings.description: The SH pre-2018 source files are Kreiswahl files aggregated to municipality. The 2008 file info sheet is titled 'Gemeindewahl in den kreisfreien Staedten und Kreiswahl in den Kreisen'. The 2013 file columns include county-only lists (BfB (Schleswig-Flensburg), FWG Kreis Ploen, Buergerliste Steinburg, UWG-Kreis Ploen). Only the 4 kreisfreie Staedte have genuine Gemeinderat results. Evidence in data: tiny villages carry CDU/SPD/Gruene/FDP/Linke shares in every year to 2013 (e.g. Arkebek 01051002, 181 eligible, 2008: Linke 5.05%, Gruene 5.05%, FDP 11.1%; CDU present in 100% of municipalities <400 eligible), valid_votes about equals voters (one vote, Kreistag style) until 2013, then in 2018 Arkebek has no party shares (other=1), valid_votes=3x voters, CDU present in only 25% of tiny municipalities. 1994-2003 files not inspected in raw, but show the same pattern (single-vote ratio ~0.98 in all municipalities). TODO.md states the SH source was 'confirmed Gemeinderatswahlen'; that is incorrect for municipalities outside the 4 cities.
findings.evidence: SH vv=valid_votes/number_voters median 0.975-0.984 in 1994-2013, 3.8 (2018) and 3.5 (2023); 2018/2023 other==1 in 527/1079 and 560/1077 rows; raw header: data/municipal_elections/raw/schleswig_holstein/Originals/sh_gemeindewahlen_2013.xlsx row 1 columns 'BfB (Schleswig-Flensburg)','FWG Kreis Plön','Bürgerliste Steinburg'; sh_gemeindewahlen_2008_codebook.pdf first page.
findings.suggested_fix: Relabel or drop SH 2008/2013 rows for kreisangehoerige municipalities (and verify 1994-2003) or source true Gemeindewahl results from Statistikamt Nord; document the series break in 2018.

verification.notes: Re-ran. SH valid_votes/number_voters median is 0.975-0.984 in 1994-2013 and 3.8 (2018) / 3.5 (2023). Arkebek 01051002 carries CDU/SPD/Gruene shares in every year through 2013 and none in 2018/2023. The 2008 codebook PDF reads 'Gemeindewahl in den kreisfreien Staedten und Kreiswahl in den Kreisen'. The 2013 raw header has county-only lists (BfB Schleswig-Flensburg, Buergerliste Steinburg, ...). Treat 1994-2003 as the same pattern (ratio 0.98), but I did not open those raw files. The codebook's multi-vote section (valid_votes counts cast votes in municipal councils) contradicts the SH pre-2018 values.

findings.title: Codebook says only Bayern 2026 valid_votes counts ballots; in fact all Bayern years do
findings.description: The codebook states that Bayern 2026 valid_votes counts ballots (gewichtete Stimmen) 'rather than the cumulative individual votes of earlier years'. In the data valid_votes/number_voters is 0.975-0.982 (median) in every Bayern year 1990-2026, e.g. Muenchen 09162000: 2020 voters 544,464, valid_votes 531,527 (an 80-seat council with cumulation would give tens of millions of votes). So pre-2026 Bayern valid_votes are ballots, and absolute party vote counts reconstructed as share*valid_votes (as the codebook recommends) are not votes. The codebook also lists the multi-vote note as applying to BY.

findings.title: Annual panel forward-fills dissolved municipalities for up to 32 years; harmonized annual panel has 62k duplicate municipality-years
findings.description: The annual panel carries each mayor forward from his last observed election with no end date. For Sachsen and Sachsen-Anhalt, whose Gemeinden were mostly merged away in the 2001-2010 reforms, the old AGS stays 'in office' until 2026. In mayor_panel_annual_harm these rows are mapped to the successor ags_21 and sit next to the successor's real mayor, so (ags_21, year) is not unique. The README says the file is a balanced annual panel with one row per mayor per year, and audit_2026-07 reports 'duplicated municipality-years' fixed at 0 (in the unharm panel, where ags is unique by construction).
findings.evidence: mayor_panel_annual_harm: 61,947 duplicate (ags_21, year) rows; 76,802 rows (27%) in duplicate groups; 14,855 of 14,855 duplicate groups contain different person_ids. By state: ST 56,424, SN 19,699, NI 346, HE 211, MV 90, NRW 26. Example: ags 03153003 (person p_03_00029, elected 2006) and ags 03153016 (p_03_00038, elected 2011) both map to ags_21 03153016 for every year 2011-2026. In mayor_panel_annual: years_since_election max 32, 26,648 rows >12 years; ST 23,241 and SN 7,905 rows. ST ags 15151001 elected 2001 still has a mayor in 2024 (years_since=23). 25,105 ST and 8,513 SN rows with years_since>=10 have no later election in mayoral_unharm.
findings.already_known: no (audit_2026-07 section on annual panel only fixed pre-election and duplicate rows in the unharm panel)
findings.suggested_fix: Cap forward-fill at the legal term plus a grace period, or at the municipality's AGS end date from the crosswalk; keep one row per (ags_21, year) in the harm annual panel by dropping predecessor rows after the successor's first election.

verification.notes: Re-ran on mayor_panel_annual_harm: 281,216 rows, 14,855 duplicate (ags_21,year) groups, 61,947 extra rows (exact match). By ags_21 prefix: ST 49,903, SN 11,659, HE 145, NI 179, MV 45, NRW 13, TH 3 (differs from the claimed state split, likely a different state key). mayor_panel_annual: years_since_election max 32, 26,648 rows >12 years (ST 19,548 and SN 6,693 by ags prefix). README says forward-fill and balanced panel, no end date. Core claim reproduces.

findings.title: NRW 2009 has no Stichwahl rows: 97 first rounds with winner below 50% are recorded as final, and is_winner marks the plurality leader
findings.description: The 2009 IT.NRW file contributes only Hauptwahl rows; NRW has 0 Stichwahl rows for 2009 but 34-133 in each later cycle (2014, 2015, 2020, 2025). 97 of 379 NRW 2009 elections have a first-round winner share below 50% and no runoff row, flag_superseded is FALSE, and in mayoral_candidates has_stichwahl=FALSE and is_winner=TRUE for the first-round leader. NRW law required a runoff in these cases (held 2009-09-20), so the winner label may be wrong in a share of them. Not documented in the known-issues file, README or audit.
findings.evidence: mayoral_unharm NRW 2009: hauptwahl 379, stichwahl 0; winner_voteshare<=0.5 for 97 of 379. Examples: Essen 05113000 2009-08-30 SPD 46.1%, Duisburg 05112000 CDU 44.6%, Krefeld CDU 39.6%, Muelheim SPD 43.1%, Solingen CDU 38.1%. mayoral_candidates Essen 2009: has_stichwahl FALSE, Pass (SPD) is_winner TRUE with no SW data.
findings.suggested_fix: Ingest the 2009 NRW Stichwahl results (second sheet or separate IT.NRW file) or set is_winner to NA and flag_decisive_round_missing=TRUE for these 97 elections.

verification.notes: Counts reproduce (NRW 2009: 379 hauptwahl, 0 stichwahl, 97 with winner share <=0.5). But it is not a data gap. NRW abolished the Stichwahl by law of 09.10.2007, effective for the 2009 elections, so the winner was decided by plurality in the first round. It was reinstated by law of 03.05.2011 (Landtag documents and LTO article found via web search; e.g. Monheim won with 30.4%, Wülfrath 27%). So is_winner for the plurality leader is correct, and 2014+ has runoffs. Residual issue is only documentation: README does not state that NRW 2009 had plurality rules.

findings.title: Other first rounds below 50% without a runoff row or flag: Thueringen (43), Niedersachsen 2011 (13), Bayern (26 unflagged)
findings.description: Same pattern as MAY-02 in smaller numbers. Rows with winner_voteshare<=0.5, round hauptwahl, flag_superseded FALSE and no Stichwahl within 70 days. Some may be genuine plurality elections or Neuwahl cycles, but the data give no way to tell.
findings.already_known: partly (audit_2026-07 section 9 covers NI 2014/2016/2019 runoffs, not NI 2011 or TH)
findings.suggested_fix: Check against the state sources; add a flag for 'first round below 50% with no decisive round in source' and set is_winner NA.

verification.notes: Own check (hauptwahl, not superseded, winner share <=0.5, no stichwahl row for the ags within 70 days): 192 elections total, of which NRW 2009 is 97 (legal plurality, see MAY-02). Remainder: NI 14 (13 in 2011, 1 in 2019), TH about 42, BY about 26 (20 in 1948), ST 8, RLP 2, BW 1, SL 1. NI 2011 is likely a genuine runoff gap (README says NI Stichwahl PDFs exist only for 2006/2013). TH cases are mostly tiny villages (e.g. Bornhagen 99/199 votes) where the source may differ, so TH evidence is weaker. Bayern 1948 are early-postwar rounds. README line on Stichwahl completeness partly covers this.

findings.title: Candidate table holds only the winner for many elections, so n_candidates_hw=1 and winning_margin equals winner_voteshare
findings.description: For about 3,750 elections (mostly Bayern pre-2000, Hessen, NRW, Niedersachsen) the candidate table has one row and a winner share well below 100%. n_candidates_hw is then 1, and mayor_panel$n_candidates is 1 and winning_margin equals winner_voteshare (margin over a runner-up who is missing). Users computing competitiveness or margins get inflated margins and a fake count of uncontested races. Bayern has genuine single-candidate races with write-in votes, so some of these may be real, but shares below 0.6 are not plausible for those.
findings.evidence: mayor_panel rows with n_candidates==1 and winner_voteshare<0.9: Bayern 3,048, HE 423, NRW 140, NI 109, ST 0, BW 9, HB/other 31; with share<0.6: Bayern 144, NI 9. Example NI 03153007 2013-09-22: 1 candidate row, share 0.518, summed votes 3,581 of valid 6,909, margin 0.518. HW candidate share sums below 0.98: Bayern 12,795 elections, BW 790, HE 576, NI 215, NRW 165, RLP 164.
findings.already_known: partly (README notes that BW/HE come from partial sources; n_candidates not discussed)
findings.suggested_fix: Set n_candidates and winning_margin to NA when sum of candidate votes < ~98% of valid_votes, and add a completeness flag in mayoral_candidates.

verification.notes: Reproduces: mayor_panel n_candidates==1 and winner_voteshare<0.9: 3,760 (BY 3,048, HE 423, NRW 140, NI 109, BB 13, ...); of these 3,732 have winning_margin equal to winner_voteshare and the rest NA. Share <0.6 in 160 rows (BY 144). NI 03153007 2013: 3,581/6,909 = 0.518 with a single candidate row, so the runner-up is missing. Candidate vote-share sums <0.98 for 13,103 Bayern elections etc. Mitigation: Hessen single-candidate races are Ja/Nein ballots (README documents it), and Bayern single-candidate races with write-ins are real, so not all are errors.

findings.title: Aggregated (N:1 merger) rows mix winner_votes summed across municipalities with the winner's own vote share
findings.description: For flag_aggregated=1 rows, eligible/valid/winner_votes are population-weighted sums over predecessors, but winner_voteshare and winner_party are those of the largest predecessor. The columns are mutually inconsistent, and winner_votes is a sum of votes for different people. All 617 aggregated rows are affected.
findings.evidence: 617 aggregated rows; mean |winner_voteshare - winner_votes/valid_votes| = 0.29, max 0.90. Ilsede 03157009 2006-09-24: valid 6,439, winner_votes 2,186 (implied 0.34) vs winner_voteshare 0.711. Dessau 15001000 1994-06-12: valid 52,275, winner_votes 14,159 (implied 0.27) vs 0.313. Winner_votes total in harm is 10.1% below unharm in Sachsen-Anhalt and 1.8% in Sachsen.
findings.already_known: partly (README describes largest-predecessor winner but not the share inconsistency)
findings.suggested_fix: Set winner_votes and winner_voteshare to the largest predecessor's own values (unweighted), or set both to NA for aggregated rows, and document it.

verification.notes: mayoral_harm flag_aggregated==1: 617 rows; mean |winner_voteshare - winner_votes/valid_votes| = 0.288, max 0.896, 476 rows differ by >0.05. README line 77 describes largest-predecessor winner and sum(x*pop_cw) counts but says 103 rows (stale) and does not mention the inconsistency.

findings.title: Party columns are unnormalised and sometimes hold non-party content (person names, 'kein Wahlvorschlag')
findings.description: winner_party/candidate_party have 7,215 and 14,420 distinct strings. The same party appears under several spellings (FDP / F.D.P.; DIE LINKE / Die Linke. / Die LINKE; GRUENE / Gruene / GRUeNE; Sozialdemokratische Partei Deutschlands / SPD). About 1,800 winners are labelled 'kein Wahlvorschlag/Ohne Wahlvorschlag' (a ballot type, not a party). In Thueringen 344 winner_party values are person names ('Geyer, Matthias'), and in RLP 178 of 1,036 values are the winner's surname ('Schneider', 'Klöckner'). Empty string vs NA is used inconsistently (ST 4,091 empty strings in winner_party, BW all NA). Any party-level analysis needs heavy cleaning.
findings.evidence: F.D.P. 148 vs FDP 144 winners; 550 candidate_party strings collide after case/punctuation normalisation; 'kein Wahlvorschlag' 1,464 + 'Kein Wahlvorschlag' 177 + 'Ohne Wahlvorschlag' 175 winners (Bayern 1,642); long-form 'Sozialdemokratische Partei Deutschlands' 13+; winner_party max length 225 characters (Bayern lists of Wählergruppen); candidate_party empty string 7,296 rows (ST 7,294), NA 3,471.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a normalised party_group column (CDU, CSU, SPD, GRUENE, FDP, LINKE, AfD, FW, EB/parteilos, other, none) and set person names and 'kein Wahlvorschlag' to NA in the raw party column; use NA consistently.

verification.notes: Reproduced exactly: 7,215 distinct winner_party and 14,420 candidate_party strings; F.D.P. 148 vs FDP 144; kein Wahlvorschlag 1,464 / Kein 177 / Ohne 175; Sozialdemokratische Partei... 18; ST empty-string winner_party 4,091; candidate_party empty 7,296, NA 3,471; max nchar 225. Winner_party with 'Surname, First' pattern: 647 rows (more than the 344 TH figure claimed). README does document that TH candidate_party holds Wahlvorschlag labels, so partly known.

findings.title: party_switch measures a change of label string, not a party switch; 37% of Bayern re-elections are flagged
findings.description: party_switch is 1 whenever winner_party differs from the previous winner_party in the same ags. Because labels change for reasons other than party change (CSU vs CSU/Freie Waehler, kein Wahlvorschlag vs CSU, list renaming), the flag is 1 for many re-elections of the same person.
findings.evidence: Of 22,944 panel rows where person_id equals the previous winner's person_id, 7,582 have party_switch=1 (Bayern 7,210 of 19,523 = 37%; Brandenburg 27 of 59). Bayern same-person transitions flagged include 'Freie Waehlergemeinschaft' -> 'CSU' (42), 'CSU/Freie Waehlergemeinschaft' -> 'CSU' (39), 'kein Wahlvorschlag' -> 'CSU' (38). 2,371 Bayern same-person flags are pure label containment (one label contains the other).
findings.suggested_fix: Compute party_switch on the normalised party group (see MAY-06), and set it to NA when either label is a ballot-type placeholder.

verification.notes: Same-person consecutive rows in mayor_panel: 22,944, party_switch==1 in 7,582; Bayern 7,210 of 19,523 (37%). Top flagged transitions: Freie Wählergemeinschaft->CSU 42, CSU/Freie Wählergemeinschaft->CSU 39, kein Wahlvorschlag->CSU 38. party_switch equals label inequality in 99.6% of rows, confirming it is a string comparison.

findings.title: Niedersachsen 2013 Hauptwahl rows carry the Stichwahl date and Stichwahl-only data
findings.description: For NI 2013 elections where the Hauptwahl result is missing, the candidate table has one row whose election_date (labelled Hauptwahl date) is the Stichwahl date 2013-10-06, election_date_sw is the same date, and HW columns are NA. Unharm correctly has the HW row on 2013-09-22 with winner_party NA. Joins on election_date between the two tables fail for these elections.
findings.evidence: Adelebsen 03152001: unharm HW 2013-09-22 (winner NA) and SW 2013-10-06 (SPD 68.7%); candidates: election_date 2013-10-06, election_date_sw 2013-10-06, voteshare_hw NA. 20 elections in candidates have election_date_sw <= election_date (NI 9 for 2013, BY 8, HE/BW/BB 1 each). 61 unharm HW rows (NI 10, BY 51) have no candidate rows.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep election_date at the Hauptwahl date and leave HW candidate columns NA; require election_date_sw > election_date.

verification.notes: Adelebsen 03152001: unharm has hauptwahl 2013-09-22 (winner NA) and stichwahl 2013-10-06 (SPD 0.687); mayoral_candidates has election_date 2013-10-06 = election_date_sw, voteshare_hw NA. 20 elections with election_date_sw <= election_date (NI 9, BY 8, HE 1, BW 1, BB 1).

findings.title: 141 elections flagged has_stichwahl=TRUE have no Stichwahl votes but an assigned winner
findings.description: has_stichwahl is TRUE and election_date_sw is set, but candidate_votes_sw and candidate_voteshare_sw are all NA; is_winner is set from the unharm winner label. Users filtering on has_stichwahl and using SW shares silently lose these.
findings.evidence: NI 20 (2019-05-26/2019-06-16, e.g. 03241003: HW leader 26.2%, SW votes NA, winner CDU), Bayern 54, ST 67. Unharm Stichwahl rows for NI 2019 have winner_voteshare NA.
findings.suggested_fix: Document in README, or add a has_sw_votes flag.

verification.notes: 141 elections with has_stichwahl TRUE and no SW votes/shares: NI 20, BY 54, ST 67; all 141 have an is_winner assigned.

findings.title: Count inconsistencies not flagged: turnout above 1 in 4 Sachsen-Anhalt rows and 4 rows where valid+invalid != voters
findings.description: turnout is not capped in unharm (harm caps it and sets flag_turnout_above_1). Four rows also have valid+invalid != number_voters, only one of which is documented.
findings.evidence: turnout >1: Dietersdorf 15266010 2006-07-02 (1.110), Dardesheim 15357009 1994-06-12 (1.161), Buchholz 15363021 2006-06-11 (1.009), Mahlsdorf 15370072 2001-05-06 (1.177); voters>eligible in the same 4 rows. valid+invalid != voters: Spiekeroog 03462014 2006 (documented), Sulzdorf 09673172 1972 (344 vs 342), Schiffweiler 10043116 2019 (8,635 vs 8,634), Greifswald 13075039 2015 (16,342 vs 16,432).
findings.suggested_fix: Add the same flag_turnout_above_1 to unharm and document the rows.

verification.notes: turnout>1 in exactly the 4 ST rows (Dietersdorf 1.110, Dardesheim 1.161, Buchholz 1.009, Mahlsdorf 1.177) with voters>eligible. valid+invalid != voters in 4 rows: Spiekeroog 2006 (466+8 vs 466), Sulzdorf 1972 (342 vs 344), Schiffweiler 2019 (8,634 vs 8,635), Greifswald 2015 stichwahl (16,432 vs 16,342; README documents this one as reproduced as printed).

findings.title: Duplicate Eisenach 2018 election under two AGS and two election types; identical counts for Georgenberg and Grafenwoehr 1948
findings.description: Eisenach 2018 appears as Oberbuergermeisterwahl under 16056000 (old kreisfreie Stadt) and as Buergermeisterwahl under 16063105, with identical counts. Sums over unharm double count this electorate (valid_votes 16,564 and 13,545), and the harm file drops one copy (Thueringen 2018 valid votes -3.7%, 142 vs 140 rows). Georgenberg 09374123 and Grafenwoehr 09374124 on 1948-04-25 have identical counts (1,755 valid, 687 winner), which looks like a copy error.
findings.evidence: 6 rows with identical (date, round, counts) across different ags: Eisenach 2018-04-15 and 2018-04-29 (4 rows), Georgenberg/Grafenwoehr 1948 (2 rows).
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the stale 16056000 rows (or flag them) and check Grafenwoehr 1948 against the Bayern source.

verification.notes: Eisenach 2018: 16056000 (Oberbürgermeisterwahl) and 16063105 (Bürgermeisterwahl) have identical hauptwahl (valid 16,564, winner 7,854) and stichwahl (13,545, 7,859) rows; Thüringen 2018 has 142 unharm vs 140 harm rows and valid votes 817,804 vs 787,695 (-3.7%). Georgenberg 09374123 / Grafenwöhr 09374124 on 1948-04-25 identical (1,755 valid, 687 winner). Additional identical pair not reported: Kirchenlamitz-area 09479129 and Kissing 09771142 on 1960-03-27 (2,074 valid, 1,376 winner), also a likely copy error; several ST 2001/1994 identical-count pairs are small villages with winner_votes==valid_votes (single-candidate), likely benign.

findings.title: ags_name varies within the same AGS (214 AGS) and NRW kreisfreie Staedte use two prefixes
findings.description: 214 of 8,604 AGS carry more than one ags_name over time ('Braunschweig' vs 'Braunschweig, Stadt', 'Hann.Muenden' vs 'Hann. Muenden, Stadt'). NRW kreisfreie Staedte appear as 'Krfr. Stadt X' (114 rows) and 'Kreisfreie Stadt X' (22 rows). Name-based grouping or labelling gives duplicates.
findings.already_known: no (issue #1 asked for ags_name columns; the columns exist but are not standardised)
findings.suggested_fix: Overwrite ags_name with one canonical name per AGS from the crosswalk or latest source.

verification.notes: 214 of 8,604 ags have more than one ags_name (e.g. 03101000 'Braunschweig' and 'Braunschweig, Stadt'); 'Krfr. Stadt' prefix 114 rows vs 'Kreisfreie Stadt' 22 rows.

findings.title: is_incumbent and term_number can contradict the observed sequence; term_start_date is not the election date for most rows
findings.description: is_incumbent is defined as term_number >= 2, but in 77 rows the previous winner in that ags is a different person. term_number comes from Amtsantritt (Bayern) or the Hessen official counter, not from the sequence in the data. term_start_date differs from election_date in 35,471 of 45,363 rows (by design: date of first taking office), which can be mistaken for the current term start.
findings.evidence: is_incumbent=1 with different previous person_id: 77 (Bayern 67, ST 6, HE 2). Example NRW 05766004 2025-09-14 p_05_00655, term_number 3, previous winner p_05_00654. Names of columns: term_start_date described in README as first taking office.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename term_start_date to first_term_start_date and document that is_incumbent can come from source term counts.

verification.notes: is_incumbent==1 with a different previous person_id in same ags: 77 rows (BY 67, ST 6, HE 2, NRW 1, BB/other 1 by ags prefix; their NRW/ST split differs slightly). term_start_date differs from election_date in 35,471 of 45,363 mayor_panel rows (exact match). README defines term_start_date as first taking office, so the by-design explanation holds; the naming is the issue.

findings.title: Documentation counts are stale
findings.description: Row counts and structure descriptions in docs do not match the current files. known_issues describes 39,986 rows x 16 cols, 7 states, 38,650 harm rows x 23 cols, 84,081 candidate rows x 32 cols, and says election_type values are ASCII ('Buergermeisterwahl'); data are 55,597 x 18, 13 states, 52,088 x 26, 113,562 x 47, with umlaut values. README table lists 55,596 / 52,082 / 45,362 / 281,439 rows and says the annual panel has 185,112 person-years for 1945-2025 (actual 281,446 rows through 2026).
findings.evidence: nrow() of each RDS: unharm 55,597, harm 52,088, panel 45,363, panel_harm 45,331, annual 281,446, annual_harm 281,216; unique(election_type) = Oberbuergermeisterwahl etc. with umlauts. Users filtering on ASCII names from the docs get 0 rows. Default fread() of the CSVs reads ags as integer and drops leading zeros.

findings.title: Berlin series is wrong after 2020 and in 2011-2015 (state parliament data with stale or shifted rows)
findings.description: The Berlin row (county 11000) is the Abgeordnetenhaus (state parliament), not a county or city council. Its 2021 row holds the Feb 2023 repeat-election result, and 2022-2025 repeat the 2016 vector. findings.suggested_fix: Drop city-state parliaments from this panel, or rebuild Berlin from the Bezirksverordnetenversammlungen / correct AGH results, and document the choice. Never present state-parliament seats as county_council.

findings.title: Undocumented covariates in the county file: population in persons and fixed over time, unlike the municipal file (thousands)
findings.description: county_elec_harm_21_cty has columns area and population. population is in persons, whereas population_ags in the _muni file and the covariate files are in thousands. findings.title: Inconsistent unit sets over time: kreisfreie Staedte and NRW 2025
findings.description: County-level files mix Kreistag results with city-council results of kreisfreie Staedte, and the mix changes across years. SH: the 4 kreisfreie Staedte (01001-01004) appear in 1998-2018 but not 2023 (15 vs 11 counties). MV: 8 units in all years except 2011 (6). NRW 2025 exists only as county-level data (53 units), while 1999-2020 are municipality level (396), so NRW 2025 is absent from the _muni file. Kreisfreie cities have no Kreistag, so a county time series for these units is not a Kreistag series.
findings.evidence: hc (cty): SH 2023 has 11 rows, 2018 has 15; 01001 Flensburg 2018 valid_votes = 27,034 equals the Flensburg city council. MV 2011 6 rows vs 8 elsewhere. Sachsen-Anhalt 2007: 10 counties, 2009: 4.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an election_body column (Kreistag / Stadtrat kreisfreie Stadt) and document the NRW 2025 level change.

verification.notes: harm_21_cty: Schleswig-Holstein has 15 counties in 1998-2018 and 11 in 2023; MV has 8 in every year except 2011 (6); Sachsen-Anhalt has 14, 10 (2007), 4 (2009), 14; Flensburg 01001 2018 valid_votes = 27,034. findings.title: Niedersachsen voters and valid votes short by 2.4-4.1%, causing national totals to be 0.2-0.4% below official results
findings.description: National eligible voters match the Bundeswahlleiterin to within 0.002%, but number_voters, valid_votes and party counts are too low. The whole national gap sits in Niedersachsen, where Land-level number_voters is missing exactly the amount of the national deficit in each election. Eligible voters in Niedersachsen are also about 1,000-1,170 below official in every year, while all other checked Laender match eligible exactly. Niedersachsen has a Wahlschein share of eligible voters of 14% vs 17-35% elsewhere and the lowest turnout in many counties (e.g. Lk 03354 at 44.2%), consistent with Briefwahl (or Briefwahl districts of Samtgemeinden/Kreis) not being fully allocated to municipalities. The cause is a hypothesis; the deficit is measured. Turnout in Niedersachsen is understated by about 2.6pp in 2024 (0.615 vs official 0.641).

verification.notes: Re-ran state sums and fetched official results. Official 2024 national: eligible 61,963,020, voters 40,114,939, valid 39,810,489. Dataset: eligible 61,962,000, voters 39,951,237, valid 39,647,269. Niedersachsen official: eligible 6,191,464, voters 3,968,780, valid 3,950,769. Dataset NI: eligible 6,190,444, voters 3,805,075, valid 3,787,553, so voters are short by 163,705 (4.1%), exactly the national gap. Dataset NI voters for 2009, 2014 and 2019 and the CDU count of 9,374,944 reproduce. Cause (Briefwahl not allocated) is still a hypothesis. I did not re-check the other Laender's exact match.

findings.title: Harmonized federal share files use a valid-votes denominator, but the codebook says number_voters
findings.description: The codebook (Denominators table, Party columns section and the 'need not sum to 1' sentence) says all federal county and municipality share files use number_voters, and prescribes counts = share * number_voters. This holds for federal_muni_unharm and federal_cty_unharm, but in the harmonized files shares are recomputed as party/total_votes, so they sum to exactly 1 and are approximately valid-vote shares. Following the codebook recipe on harm files inflates counts by about 1 percent. data_pipeline.md has a footnote saying the denominator becomes total_votes in harm files, but the codebook contradicts it and does not mention the change. European harm files keep the number_voters basis (row sums 0.984), so the harm convention also differs between federal and European.

Median row sum of party shares: unharm 0.9877 (= valid/voters 0.9883), harm_21 1.0000 for 100% of rows within 0.01.

Roughly 55 percent of rows (83,292 of 151,567 in unharm; 51% in harm) have turnout differing from number_voters/eligible_voters by more than 0.001, median difference -0.063, p95 0.19. A user who recomputes turnout from the two published columns gets 74.9 percent for 2021 instead of 76.6 percent.

findings.title: Allocated eligible_voters overstates the electorate (up to +21% in RLP 2021) and disagrees with state, EU and population benchmarks
findings.description: In the federal municipality files `eligible_voters` is the mail-in-allocated column, while `eligible_voters_orig` is the source value. The allocated column adds postal voters to the municipal electorate, so state and national sums exceed the official electorate. `eligible_voters_orig` matches federal_cty exactly, but the codebook describes plain `eligible_voters` as 'Number of eligible voters (Wahlberechtigte)' and does not warn that sums are inflated. Municipal-level effects are large (Lehmen 07137504 2021: 1798 vs 1072 orig). Comparisons with state elections, European elections and population covariates give spurious results with the default column (eligible/population > 1 in 2,004 of 8,691 municipalities in 2021 vs 10 with the orig column).
findings.evidence: National sum eligible_voters vs eligible_voters_orig vs official (millions): 1980 48.22 vs 43.23 (official ~43.2); 2005 62.78 vs 61.87; 2017 62.80 vs 61.69; 2021 62.57 vs 61.18. RLP 2021 3,703,772 vs 3,053,335 (+21.3%, state election 2021: 3.02M); RLP 2017 +14.7%; SH 2021 +8.2%; 1980 all states +10-14%. 479 of 2,203 RLP municipalities in 2021 have ratio >1.5. State/federal eligible ratio for RLP 2021 is 0.815 with allocated and 0.988 with orig. Same inflation in harm_21 and harm_25 (62.57M in 2021). The `turnout` column is computed with the orig denominator (mean |turnout - number_voters/eligible_voters| = 0.042, max 1.38), contradicting codebook line 55 'turnout = number_voters / eligible_voters'.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the allocated column (e.g. eligible_voters_alloc) or make eligible_voters equal the source electorate; document explicitly that turnout uses eligible_voters_orig and that allocated eligible_voters is not additive to official totals.
findings.already_known: partly: codebook line 255 mentions _orig columns, data_pipeline line 191 notes turnout uses eligible_voters_orig; the overstatement of sums and the codebook turnout formula contradiction are not documented

verification.already_known: partly: data_pipeline.md line 191 states turnout uses eligible_voters_orig; codebook line 255 mentions _orig columns
verification.notes: Re-ran. National sums eligible_voters vs _orig (millions): 1980 48.22/43.23, 2005 62.78/61.87, 2017 62.80/61.69, 2021 62.57/61.18. RLP 2021 3,703,772 vs 3,053,335. Turnout equals number_voters (allocated) / eligible_voters_orig; the mean abs gap to number_voters/eligible_voters grows from 0.02 to 0.085 (2021), so codebook line 55 formula is wrong for federal muni. findings.title: Harmonization changes 1990 federal totals in BB, MV and TH by 0.4-0.9%
findings.description: Boundary harmonization should conserve totals. For 1990 BB, MV and TH the harmonized sums of eligible_orig, voters and valid votes differ from unharm by +0.44%, -0.92% and -0.45%. All other federal state-years, plus state, European and municipal harm files, conserve totals within 0.3%.
findings.suggested_fix: Check weights for 1990 BB/MV/TH (likely rounding or a state-boundary correction).

verification.notes: Differences are real (BB +0.44%, MV -0.92%, TH -0.45%, SN +0.24%, NS +0.08%) but they net to exactly zero nationally (+4,678 +8,514 -13,192 +9,007 +68 -9,075 = 0 eligible_orig), so they are municipalities that changed state between 1990 and 2021 (cross-state boundary transfers) mapped to their 2021 state, not a weight error. Expected behavior of harmonization; at most a documentation note that state totals are not conserved.

findings.title: election_type has inconsistent spelling and mixes state elections
findings.description: election_type has eight values: 'Kommunalwahlen' (91,700), 'kommunalwahlen' (2,687), 'Kommunalwahl' (2,772), 'Gemeinderatswahlen' (1,109), 'Bürgerschaftswahl' (18), 'Buergerschaftswahl (Gesamtstimmen Landesliste)' (10), 'Abgeordnetenhauswahl (Zweitstimmen)' (9), 'Kreiswahlen' (25).
